hints.title: Prefix Sum Difference Target
hints.text: A subarray from index i to j has sum at least k if prefix[j] minus prefix[i] is at least k. Because the array contains negative numbers, prefix sums are not monotonically increasing.

hints.title: Monotonic Prefix Maintenance Invariant
hints.text: Maintaining indices of prefix sums in strictly increasing order allows discarding smaller indices once their condition is satisfied and removing larger prefix values that cannot form shorter valid subarrays.

hints.title: Double Ended Monotonic Window Procedure
hints.text: Compute prefix sums. Maintain a double-ended collection of prefix indices. For each index j, while the collection is not empty and prefix[j] minus prefix of the front index is at least k, update minimum length and pop front. While the back index has prefix sum at least prefix[j], pop back. Push j. Return minimum length if found, else negative one.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Standard two-pointer sliding windows fail because negative values cause prefix sums to fluctuate non-monotonically, and nested loops take O(N^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: A monotonic double-ended queue ensures every prefix index is pushed and popped at most once, achieving O(N) time and O(N) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should explain why front elements are popped (shorter subarray found for future j would be even longer) and why back elements are popped (dominated by a smaller prefix sum at a larger index).
